summary: A Time passes setting: the sun moves, and golden hour fades through sunset and a blue dusk into moonlit night in about forty minutes, the same for every player.
rationale: The change is the light moving over time, so a timelapse of a real battle shows it best: one fixed view from golden hour to night, sped up 150 times (forty minutes of battle in fifteen seconds). A four-moment still sheet from the same frames gives the outcome at a glance and as the poster's companion. Smoothness, purity and cost are measured, not shown: the fixture test and the GPU frame times are in the pull request.

capture.clip: FL_DEBUG_TOD_AT=300 FL_DEBUG_TOD_PACE=150 godot --write-movie tl.avi --resolution 1280x720 --fixed-fps 30 -- --offscreen --perf=0 --aivai --seed=3 --mood=golden --preset=cinematic --focus=0,0 --zoom=200 --pitch=-12 --cam-yaw=1.2 --nohud --quit-after=17; frames 40-505 encoded VP9 (crf 36) with Playwright's ffmpeg
capture.sheet: frames 40, 220, 320 and 480 of the same recording, 800x450 each; poster frame 250
capture.note: The clock is sped up for the recording only (a debug switch); in play it runs six times as fast as life.
